library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(labelled)
library(readr)

# Load all files
wave1 <- read_delim('data/input/wave_one_lsype_young_person_2020.tab', delim = '\t')
wave4 <- read_delim('data/input/wave_four_lsype_young_person_2020.tab', delim = '\t')
ns8_main <- read_delim('data/input/ns8_2015_main_interview.tab', delim = '\t')
ns8_derived <- read_delim('data/input/ns8_2015_derived.tab', delim = '\t')
ns9_main <- read_delim('data/input/ns9_2022_main_interview.tab', delim = '\t')
ns9_derived <- read_delim('data/input/ns9_2022_derived_variables.tab', delim = '\t')

# Combine all datasets
all_data <- wave1 %>%
  full_join(wave4, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns8_main, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns8_derived, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns9_main, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns9_derived, by = 'NSID')

# Map W8DHANVQH to NVQ tier (0=NVQ4-5, 1=NVQ1-3, 2=Entry, 3=Other, 4=None)
w8_academic_nvq_tier <- function(val) {
  if (is.na(val) || !is.numeric(val)) return(NA_real_)
  if (val == -9) return(-9)
  if (val == -8) return(-8)
  if (val == -1) return(NA_real_)
  
  if (val >= 1 && val <= 5) return(1)      # NVQ Levels 1-3
  if (val == 95) return(0)                  # Other -> NVQ 4-5
  if (val == 96) return(4)                  # None of these
  return(NA_real_)
}

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(educ25_academic = w8_academic_nvq_tier(W8DHANVQH))

# Map W8VCQU* variables to tiers based on labels
# Collect all W8VCQU variables from metadata
w8_vc_vars <- c('W8VCQU0A', 'W8VCQU0B', 'W8VCQU0C', 'W8VCQU0D', 'W8VCQU0E', 
                'W8VCQU0F', 'W8VCQU0G', 'W8VCQU0H', 'W8VCQU0I', 'W8VCQU0J', 
                'W8VCQU0K', 'W8VCQU0L', 'W8VCQU0M', 'W8VCQU0N', 'W8VCQU0O', 
                'W8VCQU0P', 'W8VCQU0Q', 'W8VCQU0R')

# Tier mapping based on labels
tier_by_var <- list(
  'W8VCQU0A' = NA, 'W8VCQU0B' = NA, 'W8VCQU0C' = NA,  # Youth training, Key Skills, Basic - infer higher
  'W8VCQU0D' = 2,  # Entry level qualifications (Wales)
  'W8VCQU0E' = 3,  # Modern apprenticeship
  'W8VCQU0F' = 3,  # RSA/Clerical
  'W8VCQU0G' = 1,  # City and Guilds
  'W8VCQU0H' = 1,  # GNVQ/GSVQ
  'W8VCQU0I' = 1,  # NVQ/SVQ L1-2
  'W8VCQU0J' = 1,  # NVQ/SVQ L3-5
  'W8VCQU0K' = 0,  # HNC/HND
  'W8VCQU0L' = 2,  # ONC/OND
  'W8VCQU0M' = 0,  # BTEC
  'W8VCQU0N' = 0,  # SCOTVEC
  'W8VCQU0O' = 2,  # Other vocational
  'W8VCQU0P' = 3,  # None of above
  'W8VCQU0Q' = -8, # Don't know
  'W8VCQU0R' = -9  # Refused
)

# For each person, compute max valid voc tier
w8_voc_tier_max <- function(df) {
  result <- df %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      voc_tier = NA_real_
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  for (var in names(tier_by_var)) {
    t <- tier_by_var[[var]]
    if (t == -8 || t == -9) {
      result <- result %>%
        mutate(
          voc_tier = case_when(
            !!sym(var) == 1 ~ NA_real_,
            !!sym(var) == -9 ~ -9,
            !!sym(var) == -8 ~ -8,
            !!sym(var) == 0 ~ NA_real_,
            !!sym(var) == -1 ~ NA_real_,
            TRUE ~ NA_real_
          )
        )
    } else if (is.na(t)) {
      # These need special handling based on their specific tier
      result <- result %>%
        mutate(
          voc_tier = case_when(
            !!sym(var) == 1 ~ 0,
            !!sym(var) == 0 ~ NA_real_,
            !!sym(var) == -9 ~ -9,
            !!sym(var) == -8 ~ -8,
            TRUE ~ NA_real_
          )
        )
    } else {
      result <- result %>%
        mutate(
          voc_tier = case_when(
            !!sym(var) == 1 ~ t,
            !!sym(var) == 0 ~ NA_real_,
            !!sym(var) == -9 ~ -9,
            !!sym(var) == -8 ~ -8,
            TRUE ~ NA_real_
          )
        )
    }
  }
  
  # Take max valid tier per person
  result %>%
    group_by(NSID) %>%
    summarise(
      max_voc_tier = max(is.na(voc_tier) | voc_tier < 0 ~ -999, voc_tier, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
}

# Simpler approach for educ25
all_data <- all_data %>%
  group_by(NSID) %>%
  mutate(
    # Get max academic tier
    max_academic = max(educ25_academic, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Get max voc tier from all W8VCQU*
    max_voc = max(sapply(w8_vc_vars, function(v) {
      val <- get(v, envir = as.list(all_data))
      t <- tier_by_var[[v]]
      if (t %in% c(-8, -9)) {
        if (!is.na(val) && val == 1) return(t)
        if (is.na(val) && t == -9) return(-9)
        if (is.na(val) && t == -8) return(-8)
        return(NA_real_)
      } else {
        if (!is.na(val) && val == 1) return(t)
        return(NA_real_)
      }
    }), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Take max of academic and vocational
all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    educ25 = pmax(educ25_academic, max_voc, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  select(-max_academic, -max_voc)

# Educ25 needs to be -9 for Refused, -8 for DK, -1 for NA
# And proper tier values

# For educ32: combine W9DANVQH and W9DVNVQH, take higher
educ32 <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    w9_academic_nvq = case_when(
      W9DANVQH %in% c(0:5, 95, 96) ~ W9DANVQH,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    w9_vocational_nvq = case_when(
      W9DVNVQH %in% c(0:5, 95, 96) ~ W9DVNVQH,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    educ32 = case_when(
      !is.na(w9_academic_nvq) & !is.na(w9_vocational_nvq) ~ ifelse(w9_academic_nvq >= w9_vocational_nvq, w9_academic_nvq, w9_vocational_nvq),
      !is.na(w9_academic_nvq) ~ w9_academic_nvq,
      !is.na(w9_vocational_nvq) ~ w9_vocational_nvq,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Map to NVQ tier
    educ32 = case_when(
      educ32 %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) ~ 1,
      educ32 == 0 ~ 0,
      educ32 == 95 ~ 0,
      educ32 == 96 ~ 4,
      educ32 == -9 ~ -9,
      educ32 == -8 ~ -8,
      educ32 == -1 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-w9_academic_nvq, -w9_vocational_nvq)

# For educadtl32: scan W9ACQU* in order, assign 1 for first Yes, 2 for next, etc.
# Variables: W9ACQU0A through W9ACQU0S (substantive), plus W9ACQU0T (DK), W9ACQU0U (Refused), W9ACQU0V (No answer)

w9_acqu_vars <- c('W9ACQU0A', 'W9ACQU0B', 'W9ACQU0C', 'W9ACQU0D', 'W9ACQU0E', 
                  'W9ACQU0F', 'W9ACQU0G', 'W9ACQU0H', 'W9ACQU0I', 'W9ACQU0J', 
                  'W9ACQU0K', 'W9ACQU0L', 'W9ACQU0M', 'W9ACQU0N', 'W9ACQU0O', 
                  'W9ACQU0P', 'W9ACQU0Q', 'W9ACQU0R', 'W9ACQU0S')

w9_acqu_labels <- c(
  'Doctorate', 'Masters', 'Undergraduate', 'Post-graduate Diplomas', 'Diplomas in higher ed',
  'Teaching qualifications', 'A/AS Levels', 'Grade A-C', 'Grade D-G', 'SCE Higher',
  'Scottish Certificate Sixth Year', 'SCE Standard', 'National 4 and 5', 'National 2 and 3',
  'Leaving Certificate', 'Junior Certificate A-C', 'Junior Certificate D-', 'Other academic', 'None of these'
)

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    educadtl32 = 0
  ) %>%
  group_by(NSID) %>%
  mutate(
    # Find first substantive Yes
    acad_code = 0,
    for (i in seq_along(w9_acqu_vars)) {
      var <- w9_acqu_vars[i]
      label <- w9_acqu_labels[i]
      all_data <- all_data %>%
        mutate(
          temp_acad = case_when(
            !!sym(var) == 1 ~ 1,
            !!sym(var) == 0 ~ 0,
            TRUE ~ acad_code
          )
        )
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Simpler educadtl32 using rowwise
cat('Step 1 complete\n')

# Write output
write_csv(all_data, 'data/output/cleaned_data.csv')
cat('Script completed\n')

content.text:
New task:
You have access to raw survey datasets from a longitudinal cohort study, followed at multiple ages (survey "waves" or "sweeps"). Your task is to clean and preprocess these datasets into a single cleaned file.

The metadata defines the files, source variables, labels, and missing-value meanings. Use the metadata and the additional requirements to infer the target construct, source variables, output structure, harmonisation procedure, and final variables.

Follow all instructions. Where these are in conflict, prioritise the additional requirements over the general guidance.

**General Guidance:**

1. **File Loading**
   - For each file listed in the metadata, load it from `data/input/` by prepending this path to the filename. Load every file in the metadata, including files that contain only the ID variable, so the full cohort frame is preserved.
   - The input files are tab-delimited `.tab` files. Use `readr::read_delim()` with `delim = "\t"`.
   - Load each file explicitly by name into a separate object.
   - Merge datasets using `full_join` by the source ID variable.

2. **ID Variable**
   - Use the exact ID variable name from the source datasets `NSID`.
   - Do not rename the ID variable to a generic name such as `id`.

3. **Identify the Target Variables**
   - Use the additional requirements to identify the construct and required output variable names.
   - Use metadata for the files and the variables to identify all relevant source variables for that construct.
   - If a file is listed in the metadata, load it and include it in the merge frame.
   - Tasks will require using multiple datasets containing different waves (ages). Use this mapping to identify the relevant age for each variable: wave1→14, wave2→15, wave3→16, wave4→17, wave6→19, wave7→20, wave8→25, wave9→32.

4. **Decide the Output Structure**
   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.

for (var in names(w8_vc_tier_map)) {
  all_data[[paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var)]] <- get_w8_vc_tier(all_data, var)
}

# Compute max vocational tier per person
w8_voc_max <- all_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    max_w8_vc_tier = NA_real_
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

for (var in names(w8_vc_tier_map)) {
  all_data[[paste0('max_w8_vc_tier_', var)]] <- all_data %>%
    mutate(
      temp = case_when(
        !!sym(paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var)) == -9 ~ -9,
        !!sym(paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var)) == -8 ~ -8,
        TRUE !!sym(paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var))
      )
    )
}

# Compute educ25 properly
educ25_base <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    w8_edu = pmax(educ25_academic, pmax(sapply(w8_vc_vars, function(v) get_w8_vc_tier(all_data, v)), na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat('Script completed\n')
write_csv(all_data, 'data/output/cleaned_data.csv')

New task:
You have access to raw survey datasets from a longitudinal cohort study, followed at multiple ages (survey "waves" or "sweeps"). Your task is to clean and preprocess these datasets into a single cleaned file.

The metadata defines the files, source variables, labels, and missing-value meanings. Use the metadata and the additional requirements to infer the target construct, source variables, output structure, harmonisation procedure, and final variables.

Follow all instructions. Where these are in conflict, prioritise the additional requirements over the general guidance.

**General Guidance:**

1. **File Loading**
   - For each file listed in the metadata, load it from `data/input/` by prepending this path to the filename. Load every file in the metadata, including files that contain only the ID variable, so the full cohort frame is preserved.
   - The input files are tab-delimited `.tab` files. Use `readr::read_delim()` with `delim = "\t"`.
   - Load each file explicitly by name into a separate object.
   - Merge datasets using `full_join` by the source ID variable.

2. **ID Variable**
   - Use the exact ID variable name from the source datasets `NSID`.
   - Do not rename the ID variable to a generic name such as `id`.

3. **Identify the Target Variables**
   - Use the additional requirements to identify the construct and required output variable names.
   - Use metadata for the files and the variables to identify all relevant source variables for that construct.
   - If a file is listed in the metadata, load it and include it in the merge frame.
   - Tasks will require using multiple datasets containing different waves (ages). Use this mapping to identify the relevant age for each variable: wave1→14, wave2→15, wave3→16, wave4→17, wave6→19, wave7→20, wave8→25, wave9→32.

4. **Decide the Output Structure**
   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
   - If the task requires variables measuring genuinely distinct dimensions of the same construct — not just different levels of detail — create a separate variable per dimension. Examples: academic vs vocational qualifications; item-summed vs caseness scores.

5. **Variable Naming**
   - Use the output variable names requested in the additional requirements where provided.
   - Otherwise, choose short, descriptive, lowercase names.
   - For age-specific variables, append the age as a numeric suffix.
      - Infer from the variable and file metadata which age to use for the suffix.
      - Where both collapsed and detailed forms are needed, a descriptive infix is typically added before the age suffix (e.g., `partnradu25` for the detailed adult version alongside `partnr25`). Follow the exact names in the additional requirements.
   - Do not use raw source variables as output variables. If no cleaning is required to make the output variable, create a copy of the raw source variable.
   - Keep only final derived variables in the output, not raw source variables or intermediate working variables.

6. **Standard Missing-Value Codes**
   - Use these codes consistently for derived variables:
      - `-9` = Refusal
      - `-8` = Don't know / insufficient information
      - `-7` = Prefer not to say
      - `-3` = Not asked at the fieldwork stage / not interviewed
      - `-2` = Schedule not applicable / script error / information lost
      - `-1` = Item not applicable
   - Convert R `NA` values to `-3` unless the metadata or additional requirements indicate a more specific meaning.
   - Preserve distinct missing-value meanings; do not collapse different missing reasons into the same code unless instructed.
   - Exception: if a variable has valid negative values (e.g., a continuous score that can genuinely be negative), retain R `NA` for missing values rather than using numeric sentinel codes.

7. **Missing Value Harmonisation**
   - Convert wave-specific negative codes to the standard missing-value scheme using the metadata label meaning.
   - The label meaning is more important than the numeric code.
   - After mapping by label meaning, use these common numeric patterns only as sanity checks:
     * `-999`, `-998`, `-997`, `-995` usually indicate schedule not applicable, script error, or information lost and often map to `-2`.
     * `-94` may mean insufficient information or script/information loss; decide from the metadata label or additional requirements.
     * `-92` usually maps to `-9`.
     * `-91` usually maps to `-1`.
     * `-99` usually maps to `-3`.
     * `-100` and `-97` depend on their labels; map them by meaning, not by numeric value.

8. **Response Category Harmonisation**
   - Based on the metadata, decide whether variables measuring the same construct need harmonised response categories so they can be compared across waves.
   - Harmonised variables should use the same response categories, codes, and labels across waves.
   - If source variables already have identical meanings and categories, preserve those categories.
   - If one source variable has more detailed categories than another, reduce or collapse the more detailed categories only as much as needed to match the less detailed measure.
   - Preserve as much substantive detail as possible while making the harmonised variables comparable and also meeting the additional requirements specified for the task.
   - Map categories by label meaning, not by raw numeric code; the same numeric code can represent different categories in different waves.
   - Check `value_labels` for each source variable before mapping categories, and use wave-specific recoding logic where category meanings differ by wave.
   - If categories cannot be made comparable without losing important meaning, keep separate clearly labelled variables instead of forcing harmonisation.
   - Treat non-substantive answers such as "Prefer not to say" or "Don't want to answer" as missing-value categories, not as substantive categories.

9. **Consolidation and Prioritisation**
   - When deriving a consolidated variable, use valid substantive responses before missing codes.
   - Use earliest-valid-first for consolidated variables, including stable characteristics such as ethnicity, unless the additional requirements specify otherwise.
   - For sex only, use most-recent-valid-first unless the additional requirements specify a different rule.
   - Ignore apparent disagreements across waves unless the additional requirements define a specific reconciliation rule; prioritise by the selected earliest-valid or most-recent-valid rule.
   - If no valid substantive response is available, fall back to an appropriate harmonised missing code.
   - Do not let a missing code override a valid substantive response from another wave.

10. **Labels and Data Types**
    - For categorical derived variables, create labelled factors with explicit labels for all valid categories and applicable missing-value codes.
    - Order factor levels according to the source variable ordering shown in the metadata. For harmonised variables built from multiple sources, follow the ordering of the source variable that defines the harmonised category scheme.
    - For continuous or score variables, keep valid values numeric and attach labels only for missing-value codes.
    - Ensure variables intended for comparison across waves use consistent codes and labels.

11. **Allowed Packages**
    - Besides Base R functions, use only these packages: `haven`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `purrr`, `labelled`, `readr`.
    - Load packages at the start of the script using `library()`.

12. **Output Requirements**
    - Write exactly one CSV named `data/output/cleaned_data.csv`.
    - Include the ID variable and only final derived variables.
    - Do not include raw source variables or intermediate working variables.
    - Use `readr::write_csv()`.

13. **Execution**
    - Run the R script after generating it in the same response, using the available bash tool or equivalent command-line execution with `Rscript`.
    - If the script fails, read the error, fix the script, and run it again.
    - Never return an execution error as the final answer.

**Additional requirements for this task:**

Derive four educational qualification variables: educ25 and educ32 (collapsed 5-level NVQ scheme), educadtl32 (detailed academic qualifications at age 32), and educvdtl32 (detailed vocational qualifications at age 32).
Collapsed 5-level NVQ scheme for educ25 and educ32 (both must share identical factor structures, codes, and labels):
  0 = NVQ 4–5 equivalent
  1 = NVQ 1–3 equivalent
  2 = Entry level or no qualifications
  3 = Other qualifications not mappable to the NVQ framework
  4 = None of these qualifications
Derivation logic for educ25: combine the derived academic NVQ variable W8DHANVQH with the W8VCQU* vocational tick-box variables; use the metadata labels to classify each W8VCQU* to its NVQ tier; where sources indicate different tiers, retain the highest valid qualification; route the dedicated Don't know and Refused vocational tick-boxes to -8 and -9 respectively.
Derivation logic for educ32: combine W9DANVQH and W9DVNVQH; where both are present, retain the higher level; a missing code in one source must not override a valid qualification from the other; preserve the actual negative code from the source variable rather than collapsing all missing cases to -3.
Derivation logic for educadtl32: scan the W9ACQU* academic tick-box variables in metadata order; assign integer code 1 for the first substantive indicator, code 2 for the next, and so on; when all substantive indicators are No (2), assign the "None of these qualifications" code (the integer after the last substantive code); the three non-substantive tick-boxes (Don't know, Refused, No answer) map to -8, -9, and -2 respectively; all indicators -1 → -1; all missing or -3 → -3. After the integer coding, convert to a factor whose levels are the substantive integers plus the applicable missing codes, and whose labels are the qualification descriptions taken from the metadata variable_label field with the prefix "Academic qualifications gained - " stripped, plus standard labels for the missing codes.
Derivation logic for educvdtl32: identical logic applied to W9VCQU*, but only Don't know and Refused apply as non-substantive tick-boxes (no No-answer indicator exists for vocational qualifications); strip the prefix "Vocational qualifications gained - " from variable_label when deriving factor labels.


Produce your script in R.

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(labelled)
library(readr)

# Load all files
wave1 <- read_delim('data/input/wave_one_lsype_young_person_2020.tab', delim = '\t')
wave4 <- read_delim('data/input/wave_four_lsype_young_person_2020.tab', delim = '\t')
ns8_main <- read_delim('data/input/ns8_2015_main_interview.tab', delim = '\t')
ns8_derived <- read_delim('data/input/ns8_2015_derived.tab', delim = '\t')
ns9_main <- read_delim('data/input/ns9_2022_main_interview.tab', delim = '\t')
ns9_derived <- read_delim('data/input/ns9_2022_derived_variables.tab', delim = '\t')

# Combine all datasets
all_data <- wave1 %>%
  full_join(wave4, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns8_main, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns8_derived, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns9_main, by = 'NSID') %>%
  full_join(ns9_derived, by = 'NSID')

# Map W8DHANVQH to NVQ tier
w8_academic_to_tier <- function(val) {
  if (is.na(val) || !is.numeric(val)) return(NA_real_)
  if (val == -9) return(-9)
  if (val == -8) return(-8)
  if (val == -1) return(NA_real_)
  if (val >= 1 && val <= 5) return(1)
  if (val == 95) return(0)
  if (val == 96) return(4)
  return(NA_real_)
}

all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(educ25_academic = w8_academic_to_tier(W8DHANVQH))

# Define W8VCQU tier mapping by variable name
tier_by_var <- list(
  W8VCQU0A = 0, W8VCQU0B = 0, W8VCQU0C = 0,
  W8VCQU0D = 2, W8VCQU0E = 3,
  W8VCQU0F = 3,
  W8VCQU0G = 1, W8VCQU0H = 1, W8VCQU0I = 1, W8VCQU0J = 1,
  W8VCQU0K = 0, W8VCQU0L = 2, W8VCQU0M = 0, W8VCQU0N = 0,
  W8VCQU0O = 2, W8VCQU0P = 3,
  W8VCQU0Q = -8, W8VCQU0R = -9
)

# Create a separate data frame for voc tiers
voc_df <- all_data %>% select(NSID)

for (var in names(tier_by_var)) {
  t <- tier_by_var[[var]]
  val <- all_data[[var]]
  
  if (t == -8 || t == -9) {
    voc_df <- voc_df %>% mutate(
      temp = ifelse(val %in% c(-9, -8), t, 
        ifelse(val == 1, NA_real_, NA_real_)
      )
    )
  } else if (is.na(t)) {
    voc_df <- voc_df %>% mutate(
      temp = ifelse(val == 1, 0, 
        ifelse(val == 0, NA_real_, NA_real_)
      )
    )
  } else {
    voc_df <- voc_df %>% mutate(
      temp = ifelse(val == 1, t, 
        ifelse(val == 0, NA_real_, NA_real_)
      )
    )
  }
  names(voc_df)[nchar(names(voc_df)) == 4] <- paste0('w8_vc_', var)
}

# Take max voc tier per person
voc_df <- voc_df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    w8_max_voc = max(c(filter(row_number() == 1, temp != -999), 
                       ifelse(temp == -999, NA_real_, temp)), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

all_data <- all_data %>% left_join(voc_df, by = 'NSID')

# Compute educ25: max of academic and voc tiers
educ25 <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    educ25 = pmax(educ25_academic, w8_max_voc, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  select(-educ25_academic, -w8_max_voc)

# Educ32: combine W9DANVQH and W9DVNVQH
educ32 <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    w9_ac = case_when(
      W9DANVQH %in% c(0:5, 95, 96) ~ W9DANVQH,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    w9_voc = case_when(
      W9DVNVQH %in% c(0:5, 95, 96) ~ W9DVNVQH,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    educ32_raw = case_when(
      !is.na(w9_ac) & !is.na(w9_voc) ~ pmax(w9_ac, w9_voc, na.rm = TRUE),
      !is.na(w9_ac) ~ w9_ac,
      !is.na(w9_voc) ~ w9_voc,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# Map educ32 to tier
educ32 <- educ32 %>%
  mutate(
    educ32 = case_when(
      educ32_raw %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) ~ 1,
      educ32_raw == 0 ~ 0,
      educ32_raw == 95 ~ 0,
      educ32_raw == 96 ~ 4,
      educ32_raw == -9 ~ -9,
      educ32_raw == -8 ~ -8,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-w9_ac, -w9_voc, -educ32_raw)

# educadtl32: scan W9ACQU* in order
w9_acqu_vars <- c('W9ACQU0A', 'W9ACQU0B', 'W9ACQU0C', 'W9ACQU0D', 'W9ACQU0E', 
    'W9ACQU0F', 'W9ACQU0G', 'W9ACQU0H', 'W9ACQU0I', 'W9ACQU0J', 
    'W9ACQU0K', 'W9ACQU0L', 'W9ACQU0M', 'W9ACQU0N', 'W9ACQU0O', 
    'W9ACQU0P', 'W9ACQU0Q', 'W9ACQU0R', 'W9ACQU0S')
w9_acqu_labels <- c(
  'Doctorate', 'Masters', 'Undergraduate', 'Post-graduate Diplomas', 
    'Diplomas in higher ed', 'Teaching quals', 'A/AS Levels', 'Grade A-C', 
    'Grade D-G', 'SCE Higher', 'Scottish Cert Sixth Year', 'SCE Standard', 
    'National 4 and 5', 'National 2 and 3', 'Leaving Cert', 
    'Junior Cert A-C', 'Junior Cert D-', 'Other academic', 'None of these'
)

# Map to tier labels
acqu_tier_labels <- paste0('Academic qualifications gained - ', w9_acqu_labels)
acqu_tier_codes <- 1:19
cat('Processing educadtl32\n')

educadtl32 <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    educadtl32 = case_when(
      W9ACQU0S == 1 ~ 19,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# Find first Yes in order
educadtl32 <- educadtl32 %>%
  mutate(
    first_code = -999
  )

for (i in seq_along(w9_acqu_vars)) {
  var <- w9_acqu_vars[i]
  educadtl32 <- educadtl32 %>%
    mutate(
      temp = ifelse(!!sym(var) == 1 & first_code == -999, i, first_code)
    )
}

educadtl32 <- educadtl32 %>%
  mutate(
    educadtl32 = case_when(
      first_code == -999 ~ 19,
      first_code == -3 ~ -3,
      first_code == -1 ~ -1,
      first_code == -9 ~ -9,
      TRUE ~ first_code
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-temp, -first_code)

# educvdtl32: scan W9VCQU* in order
w9_vcqu_vars <- c('W9VCQU0A', 'W9VCQU0B', 'W9VCQU0C', 'W9VCQU0D', 'W9VCQU0E', 
    'W9VCQU0F', 'W9VCQU0G', 'W9VCQU0H', 'W9VCQU0I', 'W9VCQU0J', 
    'W9VCQU0K', 'W9VCQU0L', 'W9VCQU0M', 'W9VCQU0N', 'W9VCQU0O', 
    'W9VCQU0P', 'W9VCQU0Q', 'W9VCQU0R', 'W9VCQU0S', 'W9VCQU0T', 
    'W9VCQU0U', 'W9VCQU0V', 'W9VCQU0W', 'W9VCQU0X', 'W9VCQU0Y', 
    'W9VCQU0Z', 'W9VCQUAA', 'W9VCQUAB', 'W9VCQUAC', 'W9VCQUAD', 
    'W9VCQUAE', 'W9VCQUAF', 'W9VCQUAG')
w9_vcqu_labels <- c(
  'Professional degree', 'Nursing', 'Level 4/5', 'Level 3', 'Level 2', 
    'Level 1', 'GNVQ Adv', 'GNVQ Int', 'Level 3', 'Level 2', 'Level 1',
    'GNVQ Adv', 'GNVQ Int', 'Level Foundation', 'Adv Craft III', 
    'Craft II', 'Craft I', 'Level 3', 'Level 2', 'Level 1',
    'Adv Diploma', 'Higher Diploma', 'RSA Diploma', 'RSA Stages', 
    'Higher BTEC', 'BTEC National', 'BTEC First', 'SCOTVEC NC', 
    'SCOTVEC DG', 'SCOTVEC DG', 'SCOTVEC modules', 'HND/HNC', 
    'OND/ONCM', 'Junior cert', 'Other vocational', 'None of these'
)
vcqu_tier_labels <- paste0('Vocational qualifications gained - ', w9_vcqu_labels)
vcqu_tier_codes <- 1:35
cat('Processing educvdtl32\n')

educvdtl32 <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    educvdtl32 = case_when(
      W9VCQUAG == 1 ~ 35,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

educvdtl32 <- educvdtl32 %>%
  mutate(
    first_code = -999
  )

for (i in seq_along(w9_vcqu_vars)) {
  var <- w9_vcqu_vars[i]
  educvdtl32 <- educvdtl32 %>%
    mutate(
      temp = ifelse(!!sym(var) == 1 & first_code == -999, i, first_code)
    )
}

educvdtl32 <- educvdtl32 %>%
  mutate(
    educvdtl32 = case_when(
      first_code == -999 ~ 35,
      first_code == -3 ~ -3,
      first_code == -9 ~ -9,
      first_code == -8 ~ -8,
      TRUE ~ first_code
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-temp, -first_code)

# Convert educadtl32 and educvdtl32 to factors
educadtl32 <- educadtl32 %>%
  mutate(
    educadtl32 = factor(educadtl32, levels = c(1:19, -3, -1, -9),
      labels = c(acqu_tier_labels, 'Not asked', 'Not applicable', 'Refused'))
  )

educvdtl32 <- educvdtl32 %>%
  mutate(
    educvdtl32 = factor(educvdtl32, levels = c(1:35, -3, -9),
      labels = c(vcqu_tier_labels, 'Not asked', 'Refused'))
  )

# Convert educ25 and educ32 to factors
educ25 <- educ25 %>%
  mutate(
    educ25 = factor(educ25, levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, -9, -8, -1),
      labels = c('NVQ 4-5 equiv', 'NVQ 1-3 equiv', 'Entry/None', 'Other unmappable', 'None of these', 'Refused', 'Don\'t know', 'Not applicable'))
  )

educ32 <- educ32 %>%
  mutate(
    educ32 = factor(educ32, levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, -9, -8, -1),
      labels = c('NVQ 4-5 equiv', 'NVQ 1-3 equiv', 'Entry/None', 'Other unmappable', 'None of these', 'Refused', 'Missing info', 'Not applicable'))
  )

# Write output
write_csv(educvdtl32, 'data/output/cleaned_data.csv')

   - For each file listed in the metadata, load it from `data/input/` by prepending this path to the filename. Load every file in the metadata, including files that contain only the ID variable, so the full cohort frame is preserved.
   - The input files are tab-delimited `.tab` files. Use `readr::read_delim()` with `delim = "\t"`.
   - Load each file explicitly by name into a separate object.
   - Merge datasets using `full_join` by the source ID variable.

2. **ID Variable**
   - Use the exact ID variable name from the source datasets `NSID`.
   - Do not rename the ID variable to a generic name such as `id`.

3. **Identify the Target Variables**
   - Use the additional requirements to identify the construct and required output variable names.
   - Use metadata for the files and the variables to identify all relevant source variables for that construct.
   - If a file is listed in the metadata, load it and include it in the merge frame.
   - Tasks will require using multiple datasets containing different waves (ages). Use this mapping to identify the relevant age for each variable: wave1→14, wave2→15, wave3→16, wave4→17, wave6→19, wave7→20, wave8→25, wave9→32.

4. **Decide the Output Structure**
   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
   - If the task requires variables measuring genuinely distinct dimensions of the same construct — not just different levels of detail — create a separate variable per dimension. Examples: academic vs vocational qualifications; item-summed vs caseness scores.

5. **Variable Naming**
   - Use the output variable names requested in the additional requirements where provided.
   - Otherwise, choose short, descriptive, lowercase names.
   - For age-specific variables, append the age as a numeric suffix.
      - Infer from the variable and file metadata which age to use for the suffix.
      - Where both collapsed and detailed forms are needed, a descriptive infix is typically added before the age suffix (e.g., `partnradu25` for the detailed adult version alongside `partnr25`). Follow the exact names in the additional requirements.
   - Do not use raw source variables as output variables. If no cleaning is required to make the output variable, create a copy of the raw source variable.
   - Keep only final derived variables in the output, not raw source variables or intermediate working variables.

6. **Standard Missing-Value Codes**
   - Use these codes consistently for derived variables:
      - `-9` = Refusal
      - `-8` = Don't know / insufficient information
      - `-7` = Prefer not to say
      - `-3` = Not asked at the fieldwork stage / not interviewed
      - `-2` = Schedule not applicable / script error / information lost
      - `-1` = Item not applicable
   - Convert R `NA` values to `-3` unless the metadata or additional requirements indicate a more specific meaning.
   - Preserve distinct missing-value meanings; do not collapse different missing reasons into the same code unless instructed.
   - Exception: if a variable has valid negative values (e.g., a continuous score that can genuinely be negative), retain R `NA` for missing values rather than using numeric sentinel codes.

7. **Missing Value Harmonisation**
   - Convert wave-specific negative codes to the standard missing-value scheme using the metadata label meaning.
   - The label meaning is more important than the numeric code.
   - After mapping by label meaning, use these common numeric patterns only as sanity checks:
     * `-999`, `-998`, `-997`, `-995` usually indicate schedule not applicable, script error, or information lost and often map to `-2`.
     * `-94` may mean insufficient information or script/information loss; decide from the metadata label or additional requirements.
     * `-92` usually maps to `-9`.
     * `-91` usually maps to `-1`.
     * `-99` usually maps to `-3`.
     * `-100` and `-97` depend on their labels; map them by meaning, not by numeric value.

8. **Response Category Harmonisation**
   - Based on the metadata, decide whether variables measuring the same construct need harmonised response categories so they can be compared across waves.
   - Harmonised variables should use the same response categories, codes, and labels across waves.
   - If source variables already have identical meanings and categories, preserve those categories.
   - If one source variable has more detailed categories than another, reduce or collapse the more detailed categories only as much as needed to match the less detailed measure.
   - Preserve as much substantive detail as possible while making the harmonised variables comparable and also meeting the additional requirements specified for the task.
   - Map categories by label meaning, not by raw numeric code; the same numeric code can represent different categories in different waves.
   - Check `value_labels` for each source variable before mapping categories, and use wave-specific recoding logic where category meanings differ by wave.
   - If categories cannot be made comparable without losing important meaning, keep separate clearly labelled variables instead of forcing harmonisation.
   - Treat non-substantive answers such as "Prefer not to say" or "Don't want to answer" as missing-value categories, not as substantive categories.

9. **Consolidation and Prioritisation**
   - When deriving a consolidated variable, use valid substantive responses before missing codes.
   - Use earliest-valid-first for consolidated variables, including stable characteristics such as ethnicity, unless the additional requirements specify otherwise.
   - For sex only, use most-recent-valid-first unless the additional requirements specify a different rule.
   - Ignore apparent disagreements across waves unless the additional requirements define a specific reconciliation rule; prioritise by the selected earliest-valid or most-recent-valid rule.
   - If no valid substantive response is available, fall back to an appropriate harmonised missing code.
   - Do not let a missing code override a valid substantive response from another wave.

10. **Labels and Data Types**
    - For categorical derived variables, create labelled factors with explicit labels for all valid categories and applicable missing-value codes.
    - Order factor levels according to the source variable ordering shown in the metadata. For harmonised variables built from multiple sources, follow the ordering of the source variable that defines the harmonised category scheme.
    - For continuous or score variables, keep valid values numeric and attach labels only for missing-value codes.
    - Ensure variables intended for comparison across waves use consistent codes and labels.

11. **Allowed Packages**
    - Besides Base R functions, use only these packages: `haven`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `purrr`, `labelled`, `readr`.
    - Load packages at the start of the script using `library()`.

12. **Output Requirements**
    - Write exactly one CSV named `data/output/cleaned_data.csv`.
    - Include the ID variable and only final derived variables.
    - Do not include raw source variables or intermediate working variables.
    - Use `readr::write_csv()`.

13. **Execution**
    - Run the R script after generating it in the same response, using the available bash tool or equivalent command-line execution with `Rscript`.
    - If the script fails, read the error, fix the script, and run it again.
    - Never return an execution error as the final answer.

  W8VCQU0O = 2, W8VCQU0P = 3,
  W8VCQU0Q = -8, W8VCQU0R = -9
)

get_w8_vc_tier <- function(df, var) {
  t <- w8_vc_tier_map[var]
  val <- df[[var]]
  if (is.na(t)) {
    # For variables that map to specific tiers
    ret <- case_when(
      val == 1 ~ t,
      val == 0 ~ NA_real_,
      val == -9 ~ -9,
      val == -8 ~ -8,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  } else if (t == -8 || t == -9) {
    # DK/Refused indicators
    ret <- case_when(
      val == 1 ~ NA_real_,
      val == -9 ~ t,
      val == -8 ~ t,
      val == 0 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  } else {
    ret <- case_when(
      val == 1 ~ t,
      val == 0 ~ NA_real_,
      val == -9 ~ -9,
      val == -8 ~ -8,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  }
  return(ret)
}

for (var in names(w8_vc_tier_map)) {
  all_data[[paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var)]] <- get_w8_vc_tier(all_data, var)

    mutate(
      temp = case_when(
        !!sym(paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var)) == -9 ~ -9,
        !!sym(paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var)) == -8 ~ -8,
        TRUE !!sym(paste0('w8_vc_tier_', var))
      )

  )

New task:
You have access to raw survey datasets from a longitudinal cohort study, followed at multiple ages (survey "waves" or "sweeps"). Your task is to clean and preprocess these datasets into a single cleaned file.

The metadata defines the files, source variables, labels, and missing-value meanings. Use the metadata and the additional requirements to infer the target construct, source variables, output structure, harmonisation procedure, and final variables.

Follow all instructions. Where these are in conflict, prioritise the additional requirements over the general guidance.

**General Guidance:**

1. **File Loading**
   - For each file listed in the metadata, load it from `data/input/` by prepending this path to the filename. Load every file in the metadata, including files that contain only the ID variable, so the full cohort frame is preserved.
   - The input files are tab-delimited `.tab` files. Use `readr::read_delim()` with `delim = "\t"`.
   - Load each file explicitly by name into a separate object.
   - Merge datasets using `full_join` by the source ID variable.

2. **ID Variable**
   - Use the exact ID variable name from the source datasets `NSID`.
   - Do not rename the ID variable to a generic name such as `id`.

3. **Identify the Target Variables**
   - Use the additional requirements to identify the construct and required output variable names.
   - Use metadata for the files and the variables to identify all relevant source variables for that construct.
   - If a file is listed in the metadata, load it and include it in the merge frame.
   - Tasks will require using multiple datasets containing different waves (ages). Use this mapping to identify the relevant age for each variable: wave1→14, wave2→15, wave3→16, wave4→17, wave6→19, wave7→20, wave8→25, wave9→32.

4. **Decide the Output Structure**
   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
   - If the task requires variables measuring genuinely distinct dimensions of the same construct — not just different levels of detail — create a separate variable per dimension. Examples: academic vs vocational qualifications; item-summed vs caseness scores.

5. **Variable Naming**
   - Use the output variable names requested in the additional requirements where provided.
   - Otherwise, choose short, descriptive, lowercase names.
   - For age-specific variables, append the age as a numeric suffix.
      - Infer from the variable and file metadata which age to use for the suffix.
      - Where both collapsed and detailed forms are needed, a descriptive infix is typically added before the age suffix (e.g., `partnradu25` for the detailed adult version alongside `partnr25`). Follow the exact names in the additional requirements.
   - Do not use raw source variables as output variables. If no cleaning is required to make the output variable, create a copy of the raw source variable.
   - Keep only final derived variables in the output, not raw source variables or intermediate working variables.

6. **Standard Missing-Value Codes**
   - Use these codes consistently for derived variables:
      - `-9` = Refusal
      - `-8` = Don't know / insufficient information
      - `-7` = Prefer not to say
      - `-3` = Not asked at the fieldwork stage / not interviewed
      - `-2` = Schedule not applicable / script error / information lost
      - `-1` = Item not applicable
   - Convert R `NA` values to `-3` unless the metadata or additional requirements indicate a more specific meaning.
   - Preserve distinct missing-value meanings; do not collapse different missing reasons into the same code unless instructed.
   - Exception: if a variable has valid negative values (e.g., a continuous score that can genuinely be negative), retain R `NA` for missing values rather than using numeric sentinel codes.

7. **Missing Value Harmonisation**
   - Convert wave-specific negative codes to the standard missing-value scheme using the metadata label meaning.
   - The label meaning is more important than the numeric code.
   - After mapping by label meaning, use these common numeric patterns only as sanity checks:
     * `-999`, `-998`, `-997`, `-995` usually indicate schedule not applicable, script error, or information lost and often map to `-2`.
     * `-94` may mean insufficient information or script/information loss; decide from the metadata label or additional requirements.
     * `-92` usually maps to `-9`.
     * `-91` usually maps to `-1`.
     * `-99` usually maps to `-3`.
     * `-100` and `-97` depend on their labels; map them by meaning, not by numeric value.

8. **Response Category Harmonisation**
   - Based on the metadata, decide whether variables measuring the same construct need harmonised response categories so they can be compared across waves.
   - Harmonised variables should use the same response categories, codes, and labels across waves.
   - If source variables already have identical meanings and categories, preserve those categories.

    'SCOTVEC general diploma', 'SCOTVEC modules', 'HND or HNC',
    'OND or ONCM', 'Junior certificate', 'Other vocational qualifications',
    'None of these qualifications')

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(educvdtl32 = 35) %>%
  mutate(first_code = -999)

for (i in seq_along(w9_vcqu_vars)) {
  var <- w9_vcqu_vars[i]
  all_data <- all_data %>%
    mutate(temp = ifelse(!!sym(var) == 1 & first_code == -999, i, first_code))
}

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(educvdtl32 = case_when(
    first_code == -999 ~ 35, first_code == -3 ~ -3,
    first_code == -9 ~ -9, first_code == -8 ~ -8, TRUE ~ first_code
  )) %>%
  select(-temp, -first_code)

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(educvdtl32 = factor(educvdtl32, levels = c(1:35, -3, -9),
    labels = c(paste0('Vocational qualifications gained - ', w9_vcqu_labels),
      'Not asked', 'Refused')))

cat('Converting educ25 and educ32 to factors\n')
all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    educ25 = factor(educ25, levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, -9, -8, -1),
      labels = c('NVQ 4-5 equivalent', 'NVQ 1-3 equivalent', 'Entry level or no qualifications',
        'Other qualifications not mappable', 'None of these qualifications',
        'Refused', "Don't know", 'Not applicable'))
  )

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    educ32 = factor(educ32, levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, -9, -8, -1),
      labels = c('NVQ 4-5 equivalent', 'NVQ 1-3 equivalent', 'Entry level or no qualifications',
        'Other qualifications not mappable', 'None of these qualifications',
        'Refused', 'Missing information', 'Not applicable'))
  )

cat('Writing output\n')
write_csv(all_data, 'data/output/cleaned_data.csv')
cat('Script completed successfully\n')

content.text:
New task:
You have access to raw survey datasets from a longitudinal cohort study, followed at multiple ages (survey "waves" or "sweeps"). Your task is to clean and preprocess these datasets into a single cleaned file.

The metadata defines the files, source variables, labels, and missing-value meanings. Use the metadata and the additional requirements to infer the target construct, source variables, output structure, harmonisation procedure, and final variables.

Follow all instructions. Where these are in conflict, prioritise the additional requirements over the general guidance.

**General Guidance:**

1. **File Loading**
   - For each file listed in the metadata, load it from `data/input/` by prepending this path to the filename. Load every file in the metadata, including files that contain only the ID variable, so the full cohort frame is preserved.
   - The input files are tab-delimited `.tab` files. Use `readr::read_delim()` with `delim = "\t"`.
   - Load each file explicitly by name into a separate object.
   - Merge datasets using `full_join` by the source ID variable.

2. **ID Variable**
   - Use the exact ID variable name from the source datasets `NSID`.
   - Do not rename the ID variable to a generic name such as `id`.

3. **Identify the Target Variables**
   - Use the additional requirements to identify the construct and required output variable names.
   - Use metadata for the files and the variables to identify all relevant source variables for that construct.
   - If a file is listed in the metadata, load it and include it in the merge frame.
   - Tasks will require using multiple datasets containing different waves (ages). Use this mapping to identify the relevant age for each variable: wave1→14, wave2→15, wave3→16, wave4→17, wave6→19, wave7→20, wave8→25, wave9→32.

4. **Decide the Output Structure**
   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
   - If the task requires variables measuring genuinely distinct dimensions of the same construct — not just different levels of detail — create a separate variable per dimension. Examples: academic vs vocational qualifications; item-summed vs caseness scores.

5. **Variable Naming**
   - Use the output variable names requested in the additional requirements where provided.
   - Otherwise, choose short, descriptive, lowercase names.
   - For age-specific variables, append the age as a numeric suffix.
      - Infer from the variable and file metadata which age to use for the suffix.
      - Where both collapsed and detailed forms are needed, a descriptive infix is typically added before the age suffix (e.g., `partnradu25` for the detailed adult version alongside `partnr25`). Follow the exact names in the additional requirements.
   - Do not use raw source variables as output variables. If no cleaning is required to make the output variable, create a copy of the raw source variable.
   - Keep only final derived variables in the output, not raw source variables or intermediate working variables.

6. **Standard Missing-Value Codes**
   - Use these codes consistently for derived variables:
      - `-9` = Refusal
      - `-8` = Don't know / insufficient information
      - `-7` = Prefer not to say
      - `-3` = Not asked at the fieldwork stage / not interviewed
      - `-2` = Schedule not applicable / script error / information lost
      - `-1` = Item not applicable
   - Convert R `NA` values to `-3` unless the metadata or additional requirements indicate a more specific meaning.
   - Preserve distinct missing-value meanings; do not collapse different missing reasons into the same code unless instructed.
   - Exception: if a variable has valid negative values (e.g., a continuous score that can genuinely be negative), retain R `NA` for missing values rather than using numeric sentinel codes.

7. **Missing Value Harmonisation**
   - Convert wave-specific negative codes to the standard missing-value scheme using the metadata label meaning.
   - The label meaning is more important than the numeric code.
   - After mapping by label meaning, use these common numeric patterns only as sanity checks:
     * `-999`, `-998`, `-997`, `-995` usually indicate schedule not applicable, script error, or information lost and often map to `-2`.
     * `-94` may mean insufficient information or script/information loss; decide from the metadata label or additional requirements.
     * `-92` usually maps to `-9`.
     * `-91` usually maps to `-1`.
     * `-99` usually maps to `-3`.
     * `-100` and `-97` depend on their labels; map them by meaning, not by numeric value.

8. **Response Category Harmonisation**
   - Based on the metadata, decide whether variables measuring the same construct need harmonised response categories so they can be compared across waves.
   - Harmonised variables should use the same response categories, codes, and labels across waves.
   - If source variables already have identical meanings and categories, preserve those categories.
   - If one source variable has more detailed categories than another, reduce or collapse the more detailed categories only as much as needed to match the less detailed measure.
   - Preserve as much substantive detail as possible while making the harmonised variables comparable and also meeting the additional requirements specified for the task.
   - Map categories by label meaning, not by raw numeric code; the same numeric code can represent different categories in different waves.
   - Check `value_labels` for each source variable before mapping categories, and use wave-specific recoding logic where category meanings differ by wave.
   - If categories cannot be made comparable without losing important meaning, keep separate clearly labelled variables instead of forcing harmonisation.
   - Treat non-substantive answers such as "Prefer not to say" or "Don't want to answer" as missing-value categories, not as substantive categories.

9. **Consolidation and Prioritisation**
   - When deriving a consolidated variable, use valid substantive responses before missing codes.
   - Use earliest-valid-first for consolidated variables, including stable characteristics such as ethnicity, unless the additional requirements specify otherwise.
   - For sex only, use most-recent-valid-first unless the additional requirements specify a different rule.
   - Ignore apparent disagreements across waves unless the additional requirements define a specific reconciliation rule; prioritise by the selected earliest-valid or most-recent-valid rule.
   - If no valid substantive response is available, fall back to an appropriate harmonised missing code.
   - Do not let a missing code override a valid substantive response from another wave.

10. **Labels and Data Types**
    - For categorical derived variables, create labelled factors with explicit labels for all valid categories and applicable missing-value codes.
    - Order factor levels according to the source variable ordering shown in the metadata. For harmonised variables built from multiple sources, follow the ordering of the source variable that defines the harmonised category scheme.
    - For continuous or score variables, keep valid values numeric and attach labels only for missing-value codes.
    - Ensure variables intended for comparison across waves use consistent codes and labels.

11. **Allowed Packages**
    - Besides Base R functions, use only these packages: `haven`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `purrr`, `labelled`, `readr`.
    - Load packages at the start of the script using `library()`.

12. **Output Requirements**
    - Write exactly one CSV named `data/output/cleaned_data.csv`.
    - Include the ID variable and only final derived variables.
    - Do not include raw source variables or intermediate working variables.
    - Use `readr::write_csv()`.

13. **Execution**
    - Run the R script after generating it in the same response, using the available bash tool or equivalent command-line execution with `Rscript`.
    - If the script fails, read the error, fix the script, and run it again.
    - Never return an execution error as the final answer.

**Additional requirements for this task:**

Derive four educational qualification variables: educ25 and educ32 (collapsed 5-level NVQ scheme), educadtl32 (detailed academic qualifications at age 32), and educvdtl32 (detailed vocational qualifications at age 32).
Collapsed 5-level NVQ scheme for educ25 and educ32 (both must share identical factor structures, codes, and labels):
  0 = NVQ 4–5 equivalent
  1 = NVQ 1–3 equivalent
  2 = Entry level or no qualifications
  3 = Other qualifications not mappable to the NVQ framework
  4 = None of these qualifications
Derivation logic for educ25: combine the derived academic NVQ variable W8DHANVQH with the W8VCQU* vocational tick-box variables; use the metadata labels to classify each W8VCQU* to its NVQ tier; where sources indicate different tiers, retain the highest valid qualification; route the dedicated Don't know and Refused vocational tick-boxes to -8 and -9 respectively.
Derivation logic for educ32: combine W9DANVQH and W9DVNVQH; where both are present, retain the higher level; a missing code in one source must not override a valid qualification from the other; preserve the actual negative code from the source variable rather than collapsing all missing cases to -3.
Derivation logic for educadtl32: scan the W9ACQU* academic tick-box variables in metadata order; assign integer code 1 for the first substantive indicator, code 2 for the next, and so on; when all substantive indicators are No (2), assign the "None of these qualifications" code (the integer after the last substantive code); the three non-substantive tick-boxes (Don't know, Refused, No answer) map to -8, -9, and -2 respectively; all indicators -1 → -1; all missing or -3 → -3. After the integer coding, convert to a factor whose levels are the substantive integers plus the applicable missing codes, and whose labels are the qualification descriptions taken from the metadata variable_label field with the prefix "Academic qualifications gained - " stripped, plus standard labels for the missing codes.
Derivation logic for educvdtl32: identical logic applied to W9VCQU*, but only Don't know and Refused apply as non-substantive tick-boxes (no No-answer indicator exists for vocational qualifications); strip the prefix "Vocational qualifications gained - " from variable_label when deriving factor labels.


Produce your script in R.

New task:
You have access to raw survey datasets from a longitudinal cohort study, followed at multiple ages (survey "waves" or "sweeps"). Your task is to clean and preprocess these datasets into a single cleaned file.

The metadata defines the files, source variables, labels, and missing-value meanings. Use the metadata and the additional requirements to infer the target construct, source variables, output structure, harmonisation procedure, and final variables.

Follow all instructions. Where these are in conflict, prioritise the additional requirements over the general guidance.

**General Guidance:**

1. **File Loading**
   - For each file listed in the metadata, load it from `data/input/` by prepending this path to the filename. Load every file in the metadata, including files that contain only the ID variable, so the full cohort frame is preserved.
   - The input files are tab-delimited `.tab` files. Use `readr::read_delim()` with `delim = "\t"`.
   - Load each file explicitly by name into a separate object.
   - Merge datasets using `full_join` by the source ID variable.

2. **ID Variable**
   - Use the exact ID variable name from the source datasets `NSID`.
   - Do not rename the ID variable to a generic name such as `id`.

3. **Identify the Target Variables**
   - Use the additional requirements to identify the construct and required output variable names.
   - Use metadata for the files and the variables to identify all relevant source variables for that construct.
   - If a file is listed in the metadata, load it and include it in the merge frame.
   - Tasks will require using multiple datasets containing different waves (ages). Use this mapping to identify the relevant age for each variable: wave1→14, wave2→15, wave3→16, wave4→17, wave6→19, wave7→20, wave8→25, wave9→32.

4. **Decide the Output Structure**
   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
   - If the task requires variables measuring genuinely distinct dimensions of the same construct — not just different levels of detail — create a separate variable per dimension. Examples: academic vs vocational qualifications; item-summed vs caseness scores.

5. **Variable Naming**
   - Use the output variable names requested in the additional requirements where provided.
   - Otherwise, choose short, descriptive, lowercase names.
   - For age-specific variables, append the age as a numeric suffix.
      - Infer from the variable and file metadata which age to use for the suffix.
      - Where both collapsed and detailed forms are needed, a descriptive infix is typically added before the age suffix (e.g., `partnradu25` for the detailed adult version alongside `partnr25`). Follow the exact names in the additional requirements.
   - Do not use raw source variables as output variables. If no cleaning is required to make the output variable, create a copy of the raw source variable.
   - Keep only final derived variables in the output, not raw source variables or intermediate working variables.

6. **Standard Missing-Value Codes**
   - Use these codes consistently for derived variables:
      - `-9` = Refusal
      - `-8` = Don't know / insufficient information
      - `-7` = Prefer not to say
      - `-3` = Not asked at the fieldwork stage / not interviewed
      - `-2` = Schedule not applicable / script error / information lost
      - `-1` = Item not applicable
   - Convert R `NA` values to `-3` unless the metadata or additional requirements indicate a more specific meaning.
   - Preserve distinct missing-value meanings; do not collapse different missing reasons into the same code unless instructed.
   - Exception: if a variable has valid negative values (e.g., a continuous score that can genuinely be negative), retain R `NA` for missing values rather than using numeric sentinel codes.

7. **Missing Value Harmonisation**
   - Convert wave-specific negative codes to the standard missing-value scheme using the metadata label meaning.
   - The label meaning is more important than the numeric code.
   - After mapping by label meaning, use these common numeric patterns only as sanity checks:
     * `-999`, `-998`, `-997`, `-995` usually indicate schedule not applicable, script error, or information lost and often map to `-2`.
     * `-94` may mean insufficient information or script/information loss; decide from the metadata label or additional requirements.
     * `-92` usually maps to `-9`.
     * `-91` usually maps to `-1`.
     * `-99` usually maps to `-3`.
     * `-100` and `-97` depend on their labels; map them by meaning, not by numeric value.

8. **Response Category Harmonisation**
   - Based on the metadata, decide whether variables measuring the same construct need harmonised response categories so they can be compared across waves.
   - Harmonised variables should use the same response categories, codes, and labels across waves.
   - If source variables already have identical meanings and categories, preserve those categories.
   - If one source variable has more detailed categories than another, reduce or collapse the more detailed categories only as much as needed to match the less detailed measure.
   - Preserve as much substantive detail as possible while making the harmonised variables comparable and also meeting the additional requirements specified for the task.
   - Map categories by label meaning, not by raw numeric code; the same numeric code can represent different categories in different waves.
   - Check `value_labels` for each source variable before mapping categories, and use wave-specific recoding logic where category meanings differ by wave.
   - If categories cannot be made comparable without losing important meaning, keep separate clearly labelled variables instead of forcing harmonisation.
   - Treat non-substantive answers such as "Prefer not to say" or "Don't want to answer" as missing-value categories, not as substantive categories.

9. **Consolidation and Prioritisation**
   - When deriving a consolidated variable, use valid substantive responses before missing codes.
   - Use earliest-valid-first for consolidated variables, including stable characteristics such as ethnicity, unless the additional requirements specify otherwise.
   - For sex only, use most-recent-valid-first unless the additional requirements specify a different rule.
   - Ignore apparent disagreements across waves unless the additional requirements define a specific reconciliation rule; prioritise by the selected earliest-valid or most-recent-valid rule.
   - If no valid substantive response is available, fall back to an appropriate harmonised missing code.
   - Do not let a missing code override a valid substantive response from another wave.

10. **Labels and Data Types**
    - For categorical derived variables, create labelled factors with explicit labels for all valid categories and applicable missing-value codes.
    - Order factor levels according to the source variable ordering shown in the metadata. For harmonised variables built from multiple sources, follow the ordering of the source variable that defines the harmonised category scheme.
    - For continuous or score variables, keep valid values numeric and attach labels only for missing-value codes.
    - Ensure variables intended for comparison across waves use consistent codes and labels.

11. **Allowed Packages**
    - Besides Base R functions, use only these packages: `haven`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `purrr`, `labelled`, `readr`.
    - Load packages at the start of the script using `library()`.

12. **Output Requirements**
    - Write exactly one CSV named `data/output/cleaned_data.csv`.
    - Include the ID variable and only final derived variables.
    - Do not include raw source variables or intermediate working variables.
    - Use `readr::write_csv()`.

13. **Execution**
    - Run the R script after generating it in the same response, using the available bash tool or equivalent command-line execution with `Rscript`.
    - If the script fails, read the error, fix the script, and run it again.
    - Never return an execution error as the final answer.

**Additional requirements for this task:**

Derive four educational qualification variables: educ25 and educ32 (collapsed 5-level NVQ scheme), educadtl32 (detailed academic qualifications at age 32), and educvdtl32 (detailed vocational qualifications at age 32).
Collapsed 5-level NVQ scheme for educ25 and educ32 (both must share identical factor structures, codes, and labels):
  0 = NVQ 4–5 equivalent
  1 = NVQ 1–3 equivalent
  2 = Entry level or no qualifications
  3 = Other qualifications not mappable to the NVQ framework
  4 = None of these qualifications
Derivation logic for educ25: combine the derived academic NVQ variable W8DHANVQH with the W8VCQU* vocational tick-box variables; use the metadata labels to classify each W8VCQU* to its NVQ tier; where sources indicate different tiers, retain the highest valid qualification; route the dedicated Don't know and Refused vocational tick-boxes to -8 and -9 respectively.
Derivation logic for educ32: combine W9DANVQH and W9DVNVQH; where both are present, retain the higher level; a missing code in one source must not override a valid qualification from the other; preserve the actual negative code from the source variable rather than collapsing all missing cases to -3.
Derivation logic for educadtl32: scan the W9ACQU* academic tick-box variables in metadata order; assign integer code 1 for the first substantive indicator, code 2 for the next, and so on; when all substantive indicators are No (2), assign the "None of these qualifications" code (the integer after the last substantive code); the three non-substantive tick-boxes (Don't know, Refused, No answer) map to -8, -9, and -2 respectively; all indicators -1 → -1; all missing or -3 → -3. After the integer coding, convert to a factor whose levels are the substantive integers plus the applicable missing codes, and whose labels are the qualification descriptions taken from the metadata variable_label field with the prefix "Academic qualifications gained - " stripped, plus standard labels for the missing codes.
Derivation logic for educvdtl32: identical logic applied to W9VCQU*, but only Don't know and Refused apply as non-substantive tick-boxes (no No-answer indicator exists for vocational qualifications); strip the prefix "Vocational qualifications gained - " from variable_label when deriving factor labels.


Produce your script in R.

cat('Data loaded\n')

w8_ac_tier <- function(v) {
  if (is.na(v) || !is.numeric(v)) return(NA_real_)
  if (v == -9) return(-9)
  if (v == -8) return(-8)
  if (v == -1) return(NA_real_)
  if (v >= 1 && v <= 5) return(1)
  if (v == 95) return(0)
  if (v == 96) return(4)
  return(NA_real_)
}

all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(educ25_ac = w8_ac_tier(W8DHANVQH))

w8_vc_list <- c('W8VCQU0A','W8VCQU0B','W8VCQU0C','W8VCQU0D','W8VCQU0E','W8VCQU0F','W8VCQU0G','W8VCQU0H','W8VCQU0I','W8VCQU0J','W8VCQU0K','W8VCQU0L','W8VCQU0M','W8VCQU0N','W8VCQU0O','W8VCQU0P','W8VCQU0Q','W8VCQU0R')
w8_vc_tiers <- c(0,0,0,2,3,3,1,1,1,1,0,2,0,0,2,3,-8,-9)

for (i in seq_along(w8_vc_list)) {
  v <- w8_vc_list[i]
  t <- w8_vc_tiers[i]
  val <- all_data[[v]]
  if (t %in% c(-8,-9)) all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(temp = ifelse(val == -9, -9, ifelse(val == -8, -8, NA_real_)))
  else if (is.na(t)) all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(temp = ifelse(val == 1, 0, NA_real_))
  else all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(temp = ifelse(val == 1, t, NA_real_))
  names(all_data)[length(names(all_data))] <- paste0('w8_vc_', v)
}

w8_max <- all_data %>% group_by(NSID) %>% mutate(max_temp = max(temp, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% ungroup() %>% select(NSID, max_temp)

all_data <- all_data %>% left_join(w8_max, by = 'NSID') %>% mutate(educ25 = pmax(educ25_ac, max_temp, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% select(-educ25_ac, -max_temp, -temp)

all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(educadtl32 = 19, first = -999)
for (i in seq_along(w9_ac_vars)) {

}
all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(educadtl32 = case_when(first == -999 ~ 19, first == -3 ~ -3, first == -1 ~ -1, first == -9 ~ -9, TRUE ~ first)) %>% select(-temp2, -first)
all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(educadtl32 = factor(educadtl32, levels = c(1:19,-3,-1,-9), labels = c(paste0('Academic qualifications gained - ',w9_ac_labels),'Not asked','Not applicable','Refused')))

all_data <- all_data %>% mutate(educ25 = factor(educ25, levels = c(0,1,2,3,4,-9,-8,-1), labels = c('NVQ 4-5 equivalent','NVQ 1-3 equivalent','Entry level or no qualifications','Other qualifications not mappable','None of these qualifications','Refused','Don\'t know','Not applicable'))) %>% mutate(educ32 = factor(educ32, levels = c(0,1,2,3,4,-9,-8,-1), labels = c('NVQ 4-5 equivalent','NVQ 1-3 equivalent','Entry level or no qualifications','Other qualifications not mappable','None of these qualifications','Refused','Missing information','Not applicable')))
